reasons: Deviation classification is correct: a cap limited to Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event is far below the fallback of 12 months' fees and squarely in walk-away territory, and 'without exception' pulls indemnification, confidentiality/data-protection and gross negligence/wilful misconduct claims inside that cap with no super-cap, contradicting the Excluded Claims definition in 21.3.
The 'Fees' definition excludes the one-time implementation charge, further shrinking an already illusory base — correctly noted in the rationale.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a single-sentence replacement of 21.1 (mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000) and expressly restores uncapped treatment of Excluded Claims; the high changed-character ratio is justified because the quantum and the 'without exception' language both had to be replaced, and 21.2/21.3 were correctly left intact rather than rewritten.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, states the playbook position and offers the flat 12-months' fees fallback; only minor caveat is the reference to a 'three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year commitment', which is not verifiable from the supplied excerpts and should be confirmed against the Order Form before sending.
